title: How Should Christians View Work And Rest
paragraphs: The Biblical Balance: Work and Rest in the Christian Life

The relationship between work and rest is a foundational theme in the Bible, shaping how believers live out their faith in daily life. Scripture affirms both the dignity of labor and the necessity of rest, offering a balanced perspective rooted in creation, redemption, and the example of Jesus Christ.
1. The Origin and Dignity of Work
Work is not a result of the Fall but part of God's good creation. In the beginning, God gave Adam and Eve work to do in the Garden of Eden:
And Jehovah God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it. -
Genesis 2:15 ASV
Work is thus both purposeful and dignified. Scripture encourages diligence and faithfulness in our daily tasks, as seen in the wisdom literature:
In all labor there is profit; But the talk of the lips tendeth only to penury. -
Proverbs 14:23 ASV
The New Testament echoes this, calling believers to work wholeheartedly, as serving Christ:
whatsoever ye do, work heartily, as unto the Lord, and not unto men; knowing that from the Lord ye shall receive the recompense of the inheritance: ye serve the Lord Christ. -
Colossians 3:23-24 ASV
2. The Necessity and Gift of Rest
While work is good, God also established the pattern of rest. After creating the world, God Himself rested:
And on the seventh day God finished his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. -
Genesis 2:2 ASV
The Sabbath commandment further emphasizes God's intent that humanity should rest:
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy work; but the seventh day is a sabbath unto Jehovah thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work... -
Exodus 20:8-10 ASV
Jesus affirmed the Sabbath principle, clarifying that rest is made for our benefit:
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath. -
Mark 2:27 ASV
Rest is not just physical but also spiritual. True rest is found in Christ, who invites all who are weary:
Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me... and ye shall find rest unto your souls. -
Matthew 11:28-29 ASV
3. The Dangers of Neglecting Work or Rest
The Bible warns against laziness and idleness:
For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, If any will not work, neither let him eat. -
2 Thessalonians 3:10 ASV
At the same time, overworking and neglecting rest can lead to burnout and spiritual dryness. Scripture encourages a rhythm of work and rest, trusting God for provision:
It is vain for you to rise up early, to take rest late, to eat the bread of toil; for so he giveth unto his beloved sleep. -
Psalm 127:2 ASV
4. Work and Rest as Worship

For believers, both work and rest are acts of worship when done unto the Lord. Our daily labor is an opportunity to glorify God, and our rest is a declaration of trust in His sovereignty and provision.
Ultimately, Christians look forward to the eternal rest promised in Christ:
There remaineth therefore a sabbath rest for the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest hath himself also rested from his works, as God did from his. -
Hebrews 4:9-10 ASV
Conclusion

The Bible calls Christians to a balanced view: to work diligently, reflecting the image of God, and to rest regularly, trusting in God's care. Both are gifts from God, designed for our good and His glory.
